comments.author: george
comments.content: Great pair of articles, thank you. I've been meaning to try Quest out for a while and this has been a good kick in the pants.

comments.author: Pertex
comments.content:
I love Quest! I have always been dreaming of creating a adventuregame for years. I tried to do this with VB6, HTML, Javascript and several adventuremakercreatorblabla, but I always gave up. IF is not a real computer language, other editors are dead. Then I found Quest and noticed, that Alex is working on it for years and is starting to create Q5. It's great to work with aslx to create games or even change Q5 itself. And it's possible to do things with it even Alex do not think of :-)
I do not use the gui or the webeditor very often, a simple texteditor is more effectiv and there is still one problem with crashing your game in the editor: inserting objectlinks like ''Bed" to descriptions.
On more thing I am waiting for is an improved uploadfunction. There should be a feature to upload your game to the sandpit without being visible for other people and the feature to upload it only for webplay and not for downloading.
So I hope, that you will work on Q5 for the next years and that I manage it to complete my game :-)
